What makes a good movie sequel?
Often the problem is that a first movie is a great stand alone movie, after which moneymakers create a sequal or a trilogy that sucks, prime example is the Matrix.

The story has to be written in a way that perfectly allows any amount of sequels. It really helps for fluidity. It doesn't mean the sequel will be any good, but at least it won't feel tacked on.

Also, whoever is writing the script for the sequel, they need to understand what made the predecessor to it any good. It's typically not one or two things that make it any good, but what often happens is that they use one or two things extensively as a crutch.
